messages.author: c3e53d7d5317214f
messages.subject: RTMB and Rcpp
parts:
Hello all, I have a pretty general question.

I am using RTMB within a package that existed before RTMB was around. To make things faster, many package functions were written in C++ and exported to R using Rcpp.

For linear algebra, I was using RcppArmadillo and the way I have written the functions, they are not compatible with RTMB. So as a quick fix, I now just have two versions of each relevant function. One written in C++ and one written in R to be AD-compatible.

I am pretty sure that it should be possible to use C++ functions exported to R by Rcpp with RTMB, but I am not sure what I need to take care of for things to work smoothly. For example, I am pretty sure that I should use Eigen instead of Armadillo because it natively allows for AD, and after browsing the code of RTMB, I have seen that many functions are using Eigen. 

I mainly want to make the C++ functions AD-compatible, just to make the package simpler to use. This is because some functions are intended to be used both inside and outside the objective function, hence C++ outside is welcome.
But just out of curiosity, I am wondering whether C++ functions would even be faster than their R counterparts, after applying MakeADFun().

Thanks in advance,
Ole

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: RTMB and Rcpp
parts: "But just out of curiosity, I am wondering whether C++ functions would even be faster than their R counterparts, after applying MakeADFun()."

*After* applying MakeADFun the answer is no! But a C++ implementation will speed up MakeADFun.

In principle you could convert all your C++ functions to templates, that you could instantiate and export for double and AD types.
However, in terms of speed you probably won't gain much. And you might have to change the C++ code a lot.

Another way to utilize your existing C++ implementations is to write your own RTMB::ADjoint code. But that's assuming you know the derivatives.

messages.subject: Re: RTMB and Rcpp
parts:
Thanks Kasper, very interesting.

So currently my function just has an "ad" argument, and if set to TRUE, the version written in R is executed.

Is there a way to automatically recognize if it is called within MakeADFun() with advectors? So something like:

if(is(arg1, "advector")){
myfun(..., ad = TRUE)
} else{
myfun(..., ad = FALSE)
}

Cheers,
Ole
